In a recent development, the countdown to Black Friday is on, and many discounts have already arrived. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until tomorrow, November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a wide variety of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected later this weekend.

Recent findings suggest that below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to revision this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.

In a recent development, apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of newly introduced and classic TV indicates and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

Recent findings suggest that the Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.

It has been revealed that do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly, ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

Recent findings suggest that apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Recent findings suggest that sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

Lego’s miniature bonsai trees can bring a sense of calm to even the most cluttered home. Building each tree — whether it be the black pine, the ginkgo, or the lilac-adorned wisteria — is designed to be a mindfulness practice in itself, centering your giftee as they go. They also make for a great piece of decor once finished, adding a touch of zen to any desk or shelf.

Industry observers note that apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you strategy to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

Recent findings suggest that rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

In a recent development, sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Sources indicate that apple’s 11th-gen iPad is the successor to the previous 10-gen model. It has a upcoming A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.

In a recent development, with 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that 007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

In a recent development, fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

According to recent reports, no one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Nintendo Switch 2 has 256GB of storage, but that won’t get you very far if you’ve built up a medium-sized digital game library. Samsung’s P9 256GB microSD express card doubles the console’s available storage.

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

In a recent development, ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Sources indicate that despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

It has been revealed that moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Industry observers note that govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

It has been revealed that birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

Bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.

Sources indicate that headspace makes it easier to build mindfulness into your everyday life, whether you’re looking to manage stress, improve focus, or get a better night’s sleep. An annual subscription gives you access to hundreds of guided meditations, breathing exercises, and other tools for beginners and experienced users alike.

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

Industry observers note that saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

According to recent reports, bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”.

Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

In a recent development, the Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

Recent findings suggest that arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

It has been revealed that nothing’s first over-ear headphones have a retro transparent design and high-end features like active noise cancellation, spatial audio with head tracking, and plush ear pads. They also feature a paddle button that allows you to control music playback. Read our review.

Amazon’s 12.3-inch Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs Android with access to the Google Play Store, unlike the tech giant’s Fire tablets. It also features built-in Alexa Plus integration, a dedicated Kindle reading mode, and up to 16 hours of battery life. Read our hands-on impressions.

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

TP-Link’s smart smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms, and lets you set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

In a recent development, google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

According to recent reports, roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.

Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

Recent findings suggest that A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

According to recent reports, the latest entry in the long-running survival horror series returned in 2026, with two different styles of gameplay (tense first-person and guns-blazing third-person perspectives) via its dual protagonists. Read our review.

The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.

The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.

Industry observers note that with a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

It has been revealed that the Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for fresh users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

According to recent reports, nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.

Sources indicate that it’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

Recent findings suggest that the Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. Industry observers note that nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

It has been revealed that compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (presently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches).

The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

According to recent reports, LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they fit seamlessly into any major smart home platform. Best of all, the smart features come at a price that makes buying multipacks more affordable than other brands.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.

Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Whether you primarily drive a car, motorcycle, or a bicycle, the one thing in common with all three modes of transport is the need for a well-inflated tire. This rechargeable 150psi inflator might just save you from a flat (or from being dangerously close to one) when you least expect it.

Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review.

Sources indicate that in Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Recent findings suggest that A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

It has been revealed that glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

It has been revealed that this innovative latest smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It will also work with the new Aliro standard and be compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

According to recent reports, the Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

According to recent reports, the Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

It has been revealed that the last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Recent findings suggest that the Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

It has been revealed that the Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of new features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.

NVIDIA reportedly halts AI chip shipments to Southeast Asia

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (396 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Companies like Dell have stopped shipping server hardware to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
  • Recent findings suggest that NVIDIA has reportedly put a stop to shipments of AI server hardware to four Southeast Asian countries.
  • In recent years, Chinese AI labs have turned to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia to gain access to NVIDIA's most powerful chips.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Companies like Dell have stopped shipping server hardware to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

Recent findings suggest that NVIDIA has reportedly put a stop to shipments of AI server hardware to four Southeast Asian countries. According to The Financial Times, a handful of the company's manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, told clients in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that the chipmaker is not allowing their server orders to be sent to them. The Financial Times reports it's unclear if the halt is temporary. The news comes just days after NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive.

In recent years, Chinese AI labs have turned to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia to gain access to NVIDIA's most powerful chips. They used a gap in US export controls by renting access through cloud compute providers that bought servers with NVIDIA GPUs inside. In recent weeks, the US Commerce Department moved to close that loophole. First by introducing new rules aimed at stopping that exact practice, and second by targeting Megaspeed, the tech giant at the center of the NVIDIA scandal.

According to recent reports, on Wednesday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its "Entity List." Companies, including NVIDIA, now need a US license to ship goods covered by US export rules to Megaspeed. Huang had resigned from his position on November 12 after reports surfaced that he had engaged in multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive that some US officials suspect was a Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed had leased access to NVIDIA chips to Chinese companies. The Justice Department is also investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules.

Under the new US rule, data centers that were already providing large amounts of computing power to companies based in China or other location covered by the rule have 90 days from November 19 to get a license if they want to keep doing so. "There's this new rule but no guidance on execution," one cloud executive told the outlet. "No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It's causing sheer chaos in the region." Demand from Chinese tech companies led to a data center construction boom in Southeast Asia. NVIDIA booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, representing a 72 percent increase from the year before.

Among other things, the contract ensures pay increases (up to $29 CAD per hour by the time it ends), an extra week of vacation for workers with 10 years of service and severance of up to 18 weeks.

Ofori Agboka noted the process was "improper [and] unfair" and that it "defies common sense," adding that the organization would take the concern to court if need be.

The incumbent three-way coalition government is led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon of the center-right National Party.

He governed with two other smaller right parties. The incumbent coalition government won 65 seats, two down from election night, final results show.

The left-wing opposition bloc, led by the Labour Party's Chris Hipkins, won 58 seats, up by one from election night.

In terms of vote share of each of the main parties, Luxon's center-right National Party secured 40 seats, while Hipkins main center-left Labour Party won 36 seats.

The official vote count was released after election authorities counted 400,000 so-called special votes.

Those include ballots cast by New Zealanders living abroad.

Preliminary results from the November 7 election revealed that the ruling coalition held a slim, two-seat majority — that's now been adjusted to the coalition falling short of a majority by a single seat.

The figures leave a upcoming entrant to parliament, the Opportunity Party, as having a preeminent position because it will decide the shape of the next government.

The leader of the centrist party, Qiulae Wong, a 38-year-old former business consultant and a political newcomer, has remarked earlier this month that she was willing to speak with either party to form a government.

Luxon will have to negotiate with the Opportunity Party if he wants to form the next government.

He said those negotiations will be "challenging" and will take time.

Sources indicate that "I want to be upfront with Latest Zealanders. These negotiations may be challenging, and they could take some time," he told journalists.

"But getting it right matters far more than getting it done promptly. New Zealanders need a government that is stable, that works together, and will last for the full term," he added.

Experts say that if Luxon is not able to form a government with Opportunity, then New Zealanders will have to return to the polls for a new election, according to Australia's public broadcaster.

#138894. Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (736 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (736 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems.
  • Industry observers note that A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material.
  • Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don’t digest everything.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to newly introduced sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

Industry observers note that A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.

Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don’t digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.

Recent findings suggest that many peatlands have been drained by digging ditches that let water flow out to repurpose the land for agriculture or other uses. That lowers the water level, supplying oxygen to the exposed peat and ringing the aerobic bacteria dinner bell. Methane emissions get turned down, and CO2 emissions get turned way up.

Sources indicate that the researchers used recent studies that measure gas emissions from peatlands to build a global model that estimated CO2 and methane release as the water level drops. The two gases respond differently to a given drop in water level, and CO2 in particular responds differently depending on where in the world the bog is located. Using reconstructions of water-level changes due to historical peatland drainage, the team ran their model starting in 1800.

The simplest way to represent the climate impact of both CO2 and methane changes was to calculate the change in Earth’s energy budget—the strength of the greenhouse effect, in other words. They calculated the total effect in 2020 at about +83 milliwatts per square meter of the Earth’s surface from the CO2 emissions, and about -9 milliwatts per square meter from the reduced methane emissions, for a total effect of +73 mW. That is 2.7 percent of the total human-caused change in Earth’s energy budget. (With the error bars on all these numbers, it’s 1.8–3.6 percent.).

Or to look at it another way, it means that around 4 percent of all the carbon that was buried in peatlands is now in the atmosphere.

Sources indicate that regionally, over half of the total CO2 came from Europe, almost a quarter came from Southeast Asia, and only 14 percent came from North America. The timing is quite different, as well, with the contribution from Southeast Asia only jumping up in the last few decades.

Draining a peatland only starts the process of releasing carbon, though. So that means past land-use change will still be producing emissions in the future. To examine this, the researchers also ran their model forward to 2100.

According to recent reports, if peatland water levels were simply held constant from 2020 on, the total change in Earth’s energy budget would nearly double, from 73 to 138 milliwatts per square meter by 2100. Moderate restoration of peatland water levels could reduce that growth, and ambitious restoration could even cause the effect to shrink slightly below its 2020 potency in their analysis. This is a process we can halt if we really want to.

In a recent development, but since rolling all the way back to the landscape of 1800 is unlikely, elevated emissions will continue for a long time. That makes this another part of the climate system where change plays out slowly, with long-term consequences.

Nature, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11339-0 (About DOIs).

FCC approves SpaceX proposal to put AI data centers in space

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
  • Sources indicate that the FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences.
  • The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.

Sources indicate that the FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real blueprint.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.”.

The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr mentioned in a statement that the action “opens a bold newly introduced frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”.

Musk thanked Carr in a post on X, writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.”.

This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent.

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.

Sources indicate that the company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s looks to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document.

It has been revealed that spaceX has noted it looks to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.

Recent findings suggest that the FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these complications. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.

Latest Update: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Watch: BBC confronts German boat dealer Marvin Reuter.
  • A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.
  • Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: BBC confronts German boat dealer Marvin Reuter.

A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

The managing director, Marvin Reuter, is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

His equipment is suspected of being linked to two fatal accidents, in which four men died.

It has been revealed that we confronted the 35-year-old at his business near Dortmund, but he would not answer our questions. He said he was reporting us to the police.

Reuter cannot be formally charged until extradited to France but could face jail time, if tried and convicted. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

The BBC - alongside German broadcasters WDR and NDR, newspaper SÃ¼ddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) - and France's Le Monde newspaper - has obtained and reviewed hundreds of police, court and tax documents about the case. We have blurred images of Reuter because of German privacy rules.

Investigators, we have learned, believe they have uncovered clear, persistent links between Reuter and smuggling networks.

Evidence has been gathered through the confessions of alleged accomplices and covert jail-cell recordings of an alleged gang chief - as well as the two deadly crossing attempts.

A press photo from 2021 - migrants in a boat from Marvin Reuter's firm (logo circled).

At least 82 boats from Reuter's firm reached the English coast in just over two years to May, according to French investigations.

There are also press photos dating back five years showing the MaReBoote logo on dinghies crowded with migrants.

In 2021, Reuter told the Sun and Guardian he felt "frustrated" and "anxious" that his vessels had ended up in the hands of smugglers.

There was no suggestion, at that time, that authorities suspected him of wrongdoing as a German detective reportedly told the Sun: "This would be like if somebody buys a Mercedes and does something in another country which is wrong. The Mercedes seller can't help that.".

It is not exactly clear when police suspicions were aroused.

French prosecutor Samuel Finielz would not comment on the details of the investigation but confirmed the head of a German company is currently the subject of a European Arrest Warrant.

The warrant was issued in May this year and relates to alleged offences dating back to December 2024.

While selling boats is "perfectly legal" it becomes illegal, remarked Finielz, "when one is fully aware that they will be used by networks involved in illegal immigration or human trafficking".

Case files we have seen say that German police had learned from UK authorities that 29% of detected crossings this year, up to the end of April, involved boats and/or engines linked to MaReBoote.

In France, five other men have already been charged as part of the investigation - an Iranian, three Iraqis and a Syrian.

In one of the two fatal incidents where Reuter's equipment is suspected to be involved, one of those who died was also Syrian.

Suliman al Husein would have just turned 20 when he died, according to a birth date listed in the files.

News reports at the time say he suffered a cardiac arrest after likely being crushed on a packed dinghy during a failed launch, west of Calais, in January 2025.

Sources indicate that he was the first migrant to die in the English Channel that year. His body was found on the floor of the boat which, investigators allege, bore the MaReBoote logo.

One night in May, French police stopped a car and seized boating equipment and fuel cans.

The case against Reuter also stems from a chance arrest when French police pulled over a vehicle with German plates, near the northern port city of Boulogne-sur-Mer.

The BMW, which was towing a trailer, was spotted overtaking another vehicle at speed in the early hours of a morning in May this year - police records say.

Inside the car were two German nationals who - according to a subsequent search - were transporting jerry cans of fuel, a boat engine, pumps and a rolled up inflatable dinghy.

The men claimed they had been paid up to â¬1,000-a-time (Â£830) to make several, similar drops to "foreigners" on the coast, interrogation records show.

Sources indicate that "Of course I knew that it wasn't legal," one is said to have admitted under questioning. "The money made me turn a blind eye.".

Take a look at BBC Verify's UK migration tracker - the latest numbers on net migration, visas, asylum and small boats.

Both men, who have since been convicted for smuggling offences, allegedly implicated Marvin Reuter as the man who had hired and paid them for this work.

Police files say both the BMW and the boat it was carrying had MaReBoote logos on them.

Marvin Reuter was arrested in Germany in May and later released, pending extradition.

Industry observers note that on the day of his arrest, German police also seized more than 30 dinghies and 9,000 life jackets. Equipment which, we can now reveal, was allegedly linked to Reuter.

The BBC was previously granted access to see this haul, held in a police warehouse at a secret location in western Germany.

Part of the haul of dinghies and life jackets shown to us by German police.

Meanwhile, further evidence has been gleaned from the bugging of a jail cell of a suspected gang chief, who is being held in pre-trial detention in France.

Recordings captured the inmate talking about buying nautical equipment from a German firm run by a man with Reuter's first name: Marvin - according to files we have seen.

The MaReBoote firm address was also discovered on the alleged smuggler's phone, the case files say.

We confronted Marvin Reuter at his firm premises. We have blurred his face because of German privacy rules.

When we confronted Reuter last month at his business in the town of Werne, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, he told us to leave and drove off.

He then returned a short time later and mentioned he was reporting us to the police. He did not answer our questions.

Recent findings suggest that we approached him in writing before and after this encounter including a detailed request for comment. In response to that request, he did not address the specific allegations but accused us of harassment.

It is understood Reuter's lawyers have challenged his extradition, citing overcrowding in French prisons as one reason. Their client should face any allegations in Germany, they argue.

Reuter's firm is based in Werne, near Dortmund.

In Germany, it became explicitly illegal to aid smuggling to the UK at the end of last year after a prior BBC investigation exposed the country's role as a storage hub for gangs. Before then, some anti-smuggling laws in Germany had no longer applied to the UK because of Brexit.

The raid that saw the seizure of equipment that was allegedly linked to Reuter marked the first time the latest law had been used.

Industry observers note that small boat crossings have dropped significantly in 2026, with British authorities citing law enforcement as a "key factor". However, illegal migration into Europe has also been falling.

The UK National Crime Agency's (NCA) deputy director for organized immigration crime, Dan Cannatella-Barcroft, praised Germany's "commitment" to tackling people-smuggling but acknowledged the country would remain "an important piece of the puzzle".

While a gap in the law has been closed, Germany's proximity to France, wider transport links and the fact that some of the Kurdish-dominated gangs are based there, means it is expected to stay as a transit point in the illegal small-boats trade.

The "vast majority" of small boats equipment in the past few years has come through Germany, Cannatella-Barcroft told the BBC - much of it made in China and having been routed through Turkey.

  • It has been revealed that 1Password has admitted that an attacker was able to infiltrate its system and steal some customer data, but it has assured owners in its announcement that their vaults and logins are safe.
  • The attacker was then able to download customers' data, including people's names and email addresses, the dates their accounts were created and their last sign-in times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The attacker wasn't able to access people's vaults.

It has been revealed that 1Password has admitted that an attacker was able to infiltrate its system and steal some customer data, but it has assured owners in its announcement that their vaults and logins are safe. On November 19, the manufacturer started investigating signs that an employee's corporate GitHub account had been compromised. The company found that the attacker used that account to access its source code and inject malicious code to its backend.

The attacker was then able to download customers' data, including people's names and email addresses, the dates their accounts were created and their last sign-in times. They were also able to steal users' public keys, but 1Password said it has no impact to their security. While the bad actor was also able to steal source code from the company itself, it doesn't contain customer data.

According to recent reports, "Your vault data, the items in them, and the keys that protect them are safe and were not affected," 1Password wrote. The service doesn't have access to owners' actual passwords, recovery keys and other credentials, as well as the secret keys that protect their vaults, so the attacker wasn't able to steal them. Since discovering the breach, 1Password has revoked the stolen token, disabled the affected GitHub account and added fresh detection tools for similar attacks.

According to recent reports, while 1Password said that users' vaults remain safe, the company still advises being vigilant when it comes to phishing attempts. It warned that since users' emails were compromised in the breach, they could be used in attempts to grab people's passwords through fake account recovery and invitation emails.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.

The change is to meet EU regulations, but Apple gives its developers more privacy.﻿.

Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google declared that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly. The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act, but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that developers have until February 1st 2027 to declare whether or not they’re a “trader” under UK and European law. Broadly speaking, Google says the definition applies if you earn revenue from your apps, especially if that revenue is regular or at high volume. Developers are exempt if their apps are only a hobby or non-commercial, or if they simply don’t publish them in the UK or Europe.

If they self-declare as a trader, developers’ contact details will be shared publicly starting March 1st, including a phone number and address. Google doesn’t accept PO boxes for developer payment profile addresses, meaning many independent developers without an office will either have to share their home address online or pay for a registered agent or other service that provides a business address. One independent developer told The Elec they were considering renting a private office solely to comply with the new rules. We’ve asked Google to confirm why developers aren’t permitted to publish a PO box address, and why details are being shared globally, and will update this article when we hear back.

According to recent reports, apple is subject to the same regulations, but is handling them differently to Google. It will only display developer addresses within the relevant European countries, rather than publishing them worldwide. It’s also allowing developers to supply PO box addresses, so long as they provide Apple with a receipt or bill that links the PO box to their regular address.

Patch, November 26th: Added mention of developers’ option to use a registered agent service for a business address.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These are our rolling updates from India on Friday, November 27:.

A brief sitting of the Indian parliament will take place after the monsoon session was adjourned indefinitely back in August.

India's Lok Sabha is set to meet on Monday.

The Rajya Sabha will resume proceedings on Wednesday.

India's main opposition Congress party has deemed the move by Modi's government to call for the brief sitting of the parliament "an assault on the Constitution of India" which Congress General Secretary in-charge Communications and MP Jairam Ramesh said "must and will be resisted with all might.".

In a post on X, Ramesh accused the government of "moving to manufacture a fraudulent two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha".

Ramesh also listed out a three-point  Congress stance on delimitation and women's quota, which includes:.

A meeting of the Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group is also expected to be held on Saturday to discuss the gameplan for the upcoming parliament sitting, news agency ANI reported.

A political storm could be on the horizon in India as both houses of India's bicameral parliament are set to reconvene next week for a special sitting at the request of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

The Lok Sabha (lower house) is slated to sit on November 30 while the Rajya Sabha (upper house) will meet on December 2, official memos said, adding that the session may conclude on December 3.

"The Government has requested Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha and Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha to reconvene Lok Sabha on Monday, 30th November, 2026 and Rajya Sabha on Wednesday, 2nd December, 2026 respectively to transact essential Government Business," Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju wrote on X, announcing the government's request on Thursday evening.

The resumption of parliament comes after the monsoon session, which is the second regular session of India's legislative body, saw both the houses being adjourned sine die (indefinitely) on August 13.

The session never ended formally and has remained unprorogued for a record over 100 days, while a winter session that typically starts early December looks delayed.

The monsoon session was turbulent as it began amid a massive youth-led protest called by India's "Cockroach" movement that sought, and later managed to get, the resignation of Modi's then-education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam irregularities.

The parliament, itself, became a protest ground as both Modi's ruling coalition, led by his Bharatiya Janata Party, and the opposition INDIA bloc, by Congress, held demonstrations within its premises.

The political deadlock was unrelenting and the parliament struggled to get much business underway, culminating in the adjournment.

This is Dharvi Vaid Dhulia from DW's bureau in Upcoming Delhi, back with your daily dose of news from India.

Here is what's creating a buzz in the world's largest democracy this morning:.

Indian lawmakers are making their way back to the parliament next week, more than three months after a rocky — and not formal — conclusion of the monsoon session of the country's supreme legislative body which struggled to conduct its business amid an outpouring of protests against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government over student challenges.

The Modi government's request to reconvene both houses of the parliament for a special sitting has been accepted, with parliamentarians huddling in the Lok Sabha  — the lower house — on November 30 and Rajya Sabha —  the upper house — on December 2.

The ruling coalition has not explicitly stated what affairs it wants to discuss during the short session and has only noted it wants to "transact essential government business.".

However, speculation is rife that Modi's government could once again push a package of defeated bills  — including a contentious population-based redrawing of voting boundaries and a women's quota  intertwined with it.

Sources indicate that and in the world of cricket,  it is day one of the second test match between India and Fresh Zealand in Christchurch's Hagley Oval . Both teams are vying for a series win in this final match after the first one in Wellington ended in a draw.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the tech giant’s management and governance practices.
  • Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement.
  • The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the tech giant’s management and governance practices.

Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement.

The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.

Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral.

In August, Nvidia declared plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported.

A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The website does not store payment, government ID or financial information, so none of that was exposed.

Recent findings suggest that video game-logging site Backloggd has urged users to change their passwords after announcing a security breach. The website's administrator MrProg wrote in a post dated November 25 that "someone exploited a bug in Backloggd to gain access to the site's admin tools." As a result, the infiltrator was able to access usernames, email addresses, hashed passwords and the IP addresses users signed in from. Payment information was not affected as that's handled through Patreon.

It has been revealed that backloggd admin MrProg mentioned that, while the platform uses "a strong hashing method" to mask login credentials, "weak or common passwords can sometimes be guessed from their hashes." As such, it's best for Backlogged users to change their password for the site and anywhere else they use the same one. (Take this as a reminder to opt for a strong, unique password on every single service you use. A password manager can help handle that, while passkeys and multi-factor authentication add extra layers of security to your accounts.).

According to recent reports, mrProg apologized for the security incident. The admin took Backloggd offline as soon as they became aware of the situation to fix the bug and lock out the attacker, who also hid games and restricted some accounts. All consumers will need to log back in, and MrProg said they're reverting all the changes the attacker made.

According to recent reports, "Your game logs, reviews and lists all remain intact," MrProg added. "I'm right now seeking legal guidance to ensure I handle this with absolute care and will share a full notice with more details soon." The site's operator has "already added stricter access to the admin tools and will continue to commit to stronger security features to help protect your account.".

Sources indicate that backloggd is a site on which people can log and rate games they play, in a similar fashion to what Letterboxd does for movies. Consumers can track their game collection, review what they've played, create lists and follow their friends' gaming progress. Backloggd has been around for eight years and it hit 1 million users this month. A native mobile app is coming next year. Those who back the site via Patreon can now check out a beta version of the Android app.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If the ruling bloc cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.

New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters.

Recent findings suggest that it now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.

The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and Newly introduced Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively.

A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it.

Luxon on Friday acknowledged that negotiations "may be challenging" and will take some time.

"Kiwis won't thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart or for sending them back to the polls," he told reporters.

Sources indicate that labour leader Chris Hipkins mentioned his party "ran an incredible campaign" but acknowledged that it doesn't have negotiating power despite winning the popular vote. "More New Zealanders voted for change at this election than for the status quo," he said.

Latest Zealand's mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each person casts two votes â one for their preferred political party and another for their choice of local representative.

Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te PÄti MÄori, which represents MÄori interests, picked up five.

Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. Opportunity's leader Qiulae Wong told reporters her party will negotiate with National, but that all options remain on the table.

It has been revealed that "There are seven parties in parliment and everyone is responsible for making sure we do everything we can to deliver a stable government for New Zealand. It's not just up to us," she noted on Friday.

Preliminary results on 7 November, election day, had projected that National combined with its coalition partners would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc.

But today's official tally indicates it had lost two seats on special votes - cast by citizens who were overseas or outside of their registered electorate on election day - which typically skew left.

Some of National's key election pledges include lower taxes, cheaper energy, more renewable generation, and a greater focus on defence.

Labour, meanwhile, had campaigned to cut healthcare, public transport and fuel costs, more government support for social housing, among other things.

In earlier interviews with the BBC, many voters had expressed frustration over spiralling costs of living and high unemployment across the country, with declining faith in their political leadership.

"There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread," said 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger.

A 40-year-old man said he didn't vote as he could not bring himself to tick any of the boxes on the ballot paper.

More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to a survey by the Helen Clark Foundation, a public policy think tank.

Kiwis have been leaving the country in record numbers, with many of them, including former prime minister Jacinda Arden, moving to Australia.

    Industry observers note that kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

    #138871. Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (491 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car.
    • “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” mentioned Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program.
    • Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win. Now it wants another shot at the really substantial trophy, and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41.

    “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” mentioned Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It’s the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.”.

    Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura.

    According to recent reports, the hybrid system and transmission are also standard parts. But Ford supplies the engine—a 5.4 L V8 based on the Mustang’s Coyote engine—as well as software to control the hybrid powertrain. A non-hybridized version of the Coyote has already been racing effectively under the hood of the Ford Mustang GT3.

    The technical regulations also allow for more styling freedom than we often see in racing. The absolute amount of aerodynamic downforce is capped, as is the minimum drag, so OEMs are encouraged to use road car styling details to create a closer link between prototype and road car. I’ll probably need to spend more time looking at it to spot those road car cues, but I do see quite a few superficial similarities with the Genesis LMDh car, as well as the Ferrari Hypercar.

    Despite being an American car brand, Ford doesn’t have prepares as yet to enter IMSA’s WeatherTech championship, so don’t expect to see the GT41 next January racing at Daytona. Instead, it will take its first green flag in Qatar in March, the first of WEC’s nine races next season.

    Ford should find it an extremely competitive championship. Although Peugeot and Alpine will not race next year, McLaren is also entering, alongside returning teams from Aston Martin, BMW, Cadillac, Genesis, Ferrari, and Toyota, which this year won Le Mans and the overall title, following three years of Ferrari domination.

    #138870. Industry News: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1318 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1318 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, it should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype.
    • GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ($2 billion).
    • The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, it should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.

    GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ($2 billion).

    The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.

    Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda, who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.”.

    Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids.

    “We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder, managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent organization Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.

    That’s because GTA VI was created entirely without generative AI.

    “We’re kind of at this technological moment where this way of developing has sort of reached its natural frontier,” Feder mentioned. “I don’t think you can say that games like this will always be around.”.

    Recent findings suggest that as millions of people immersed themselves in Vice City, the tech industry witnessed another long-awaited moment: Anthropic became the first major AI lab to go public. At Nasdaq HQ, Anthropic executives gathered to celebrate the Claude maker’s $81.3 billion IPO. At virtually the same moment that Anthropic broke the record for the largest IPO ever, GTA VI was also breaking records with the highest-rated and best-selling game launch of all time.

    But when the Anthropic team rang the bell on Thursday, the sound also signaled the end of an era in video game development, and perhaps even in the arts at large.

    According to recent reports, the AI industry operates with efficiency as its north star. The promise of this technology is that we will be able to automate so much work that we can expand the capabilities of humanity, avoiding needless time spent tinkering with ultimately fruitless ideas. Instead, a prompt goes into an LLM, and a response is spat out.

    This technological revolution exploded into the world with some soul-crushing side effects: children are inundated with mind-numbing slop on YouTube, lawyers cite nonexistent cases in court, and tech companies like Meta lay off tens of thousands of people as part of a corporate-branded “Year of Efficiency.” But against the backdrop of the AI industry’s first major IPO, Rockstar has unveiled a game that about 5,000 people labored over for more than a decade.

    The final product is breathtaking, looking so lifelike that it can be hard to distinguish gameplay footage from real life. These sprawling open-world games are usually made possible by procedurally generating new landscapes and objects, but Rockstar has taken the time to painstakingly craft every detail of the world, even developing 30,000 different nonplayable characters with unique appearances and personalities.

    The video game industry is already grappling with the threat of AI. Google’s Project Genie, which launched earlier this year, allows owners to create and wander around 3D worlds generated from prompts to an LLM. The stock prices of several video game companies faltered around the time of Project Genie’s release, perhaps because of investors’ uncertainty about the future relevance of video game developers.

    Recent findings suggest that “The notion that somehow new tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world, it’s a laughable notion,” Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick noted at the time. “It’s just never been the case with entertainment.”.

    Zelnick’s fellow tech CEOs see different future, though. On a Meta earnings call this year, CEO Mark Zuckerberg promised that, “soon, you’ll have an AI that understands you and [can] even generate great personalized content for you.”.

    Elon Musk even went as far as proposing that a game like GTA VI could be made with AI.

    Industry observers note that “You won’t even have to ask,” Musk wrote on X. “AI will figure what video game you’d like best.”.

    This is the paradox of “Grandthropic” week. GTA VI is so impressively vast and captivating because its developers could make mistakes, experiment, and rework ideas, even if that meant delaying the game (twice). GTA VI was incubated with the exact inefficiencies that investors hope AI companies like Anthropic can help eradicate.

    “Plenty of fantastic art — video games and elsewhere — almost by definition has to be created slowly, and there’s something to having that kind of inefficiency around it,” Feder noted. “Creative output requires deletion, right? Getting to kind of a masterpiece oftentimes requires an enormous amount of deletion. And when you’re talking about a game of the kind of complexity we’re talking about, that kind of deletion ends up being very expensive, and it is by definition not efficient.”.

    GTA VI reeks of its own humanity – every small detail is loaded with intention, but it’s this impressive precision that keeps the world abuzz, triggering the kind of monocultural moment that has become increasingly rare in a media landscape that revolves around highly personalized social media algorithms.

    The game forces the player to slow down, which is either frustrating or genius, depending on your sense of humor. People waited more than three presidential terms for the next installment in a high-octane action franchise, only to download a 212 GB behemoth of a game in which your earliest missions involve driving around doing errands and putting up drywall to make your girlfriend happy. Don’t worry — there are still car chases and shootouts — but in a moment when AI feels suffocating, GTA VI is such an artistic achievement that it is reaching audiences that don’t even like violent video games.

    The ultimate fantasy of GTA VI is no longer to role-play as a criminal — the fantasy is just taking your time to relish the mundane and explore an expansive world that developers were given the time and space to perfect.
